executiveSummary: GM0534's official 2025 identity, population, neighbourhood, place and safety-region inputs reconcile, and the complete deterministic model gate passes. Release nevertheless remains correction-required. The coastal preset reaches 0.618867 peak severity, an internal depth-like inundation-stress field of 2.066345 and 12,528 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without selecting a North Sea defence/breach, Rijnland boezem or Ringvaart pathway, hydraulic footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial T+24 similarly produces 0.630445 inundation stress and 4,813 affected without a sewer catchment, terrain or event-valid pump/culvert state. The exact-zero named-major-river result is only a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel screen and is not an all-clear for the Ringvaart, boezem, regional kades, polders, groundwater or sewers. Seven unrelated hazards reuse the same complete twenty-two-neighbourhood order. The four-edge road proxy mislabels the north boundary connection to Bloemendaal as N206 while the official risk profile identifies N208 as decisive for accessibility; rail, Ringvaart crossing state and modal alternatives do not carry operations. Public water assets, electricity planning, antennas, care, education, transport and external-safety records are useful context but do not establish live connectivity, occupancy, capacity, backup or recovery. Unknown and NoData must never be rendered as zero or safe, and every first-72-hour consequence must remain a transparent exercise output until event-valid evidence supports it.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0534 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood and place geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; deployment retrieval 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0534 as Hillegom and reports 22,786 residents, density 1,773/km², 22.0% aged 65 or older and 3,691 one-person households; the generated centre is inside the 2025 boundary.

Twenty-two published neighbourhood rows sum to 22,800 residents, fourteen above the municipality total (+0.061%); households sum to 10,340 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 5,035. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 22,786 without rewriting observations.

One active BAG woonplaats and one BRT woonkern are named Hillegom. BAG/PDOK place context is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and independently versioned from generalized CBS polygons; labels are not flood compartments, sewer catchments, service areas or present-person footprints.

CBS null, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values remain NoData. Registered residents exclude commuters, station passengers, event visitors, labour migrants not registered at the address, pupils, care visitors and responders.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023-2026: municipality Hillegom and crisis plan 2024-2027
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2023-2026; crisis plan December 2024; pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official municipality page identifies the annual Bloemencorso, Hillegom station, difficult-to-reach locations and the particular influence of N208 on accessibility.

It identifies labour migrants, refugees, longer-at-home older people and less-self-reliant people as complex-fire concerns and identifies Draka Interfoam as a BRZO/Seveso company requiring continued responder preparedness.

The profile lists flood, nature fire, extreme weather, hazardous substances, rail/road/water incidents and gas, electricity, drinking-water, sewer, telecom, waste and food interruptions as relevant crisis types. It says climate change can increase flood likelihood and impact.

The regional risk profile and crisis plan are official multi-year qualitative planning evidence, not a live incident, warning, route state, facility inventory, plume, occupancy, resource level, probability or restoration commitment. No standard machine cadence or blanket reuse licence was stated.

evidenceSources.title: Programma Water en Klimaatadaptatie 2024-2028 and current Water in Hillegom guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Programme adopted 2023 for 2024-2028; current municipal water page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted programme covers water nuisance, drought, heat, flood and water quality and assigns measures for culverts, banks, dredging and integrated urban water management with Rijnland. The official council PDF was publicly indexed but returned HTTP 403 to the audit client, so only public official metadata and indexed text were used.

The current municipal page defines the urban system as sewers, public space and surface water handling wastewater, groundwater and storm water. It says extreme rain can leave streets holding water because sewers are not designed for extreme downpours and that heavy-rain overflows can reduce surface-water oxygen.

Municipal responsibilities include wastewater collection/transport, storm-water processing and mitigation of groundwater nuisance through sewers, pumps, drainage and surface water. This establishes mechanisms and responsibilities, not a live hydraulic network or event-time state.

No reusable event-depth raster/API, native resolution, full catchment topology, fixed refresh cadence, blanket licence, pump telemetry, culvert status or NoData contract was established; missing detail remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: Rijnland boezem, Ringvaart peak storage and seasonal De Zilk water-level controls
evidenceSources.edition: Current public pages inspected 3 September 2026; De Zilk notice dated 3 April 2026
supports: Rijnland states that the Ringvaart Haarlemmermeer belongs to its boezem and that the current boezem system does not meet the legal water-nuisance standard; prolonged heavy rain can raise the central system enough to overtop a boezem kade.

The Haarlemmermeer peak storage is designed for one million cubic metres and expected use about once per fifteen years. A decision depends on current water-level rise, forecast rain, saturated soil, wind setup and expected damage, demonstrating event-specific state rather than a municipality scalar.

The current page records that a November 2024 test found a repaired leak and sand-carrying boils that can weaken the dike and that further tests await clarified measures; operational readiness therefore requires dated confirmation and must not be inferred from the design description.

Rijnland's 3 April 2026 notice says De Zilk compartment boards were removed on 8-9 April, restoring a boezem connection from 10 April, while boards return and the area is pumped down in winter for bulb cultivation. Seasonal configuration and validity time materially affect Hillegom pathways and navigation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards; Rijkswaterstaat/WMCN
evidenceSources.title: IMWA/DAMO water assets and LIWO flood-scenario catalogue
evidenceSources.edition: HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: The CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation assigns 24 realized points to GM0534 by full 2025 CBS boundary containment: three DWA/RWA sewer pumps, eighteen surface-water pumps and three sluices. Contributor completeness is explicitly partial.

Named records include AWTG Zanderijpolder, Elsbroek and Vosselaan and multiple Rijnland polder pumps/underdrainage and De Zilk sluices. A registered point or numeric capacity does not establish connected catchment, compatible units, flow direction, telemetry, operating state, power/backup, condition, crew or restoration.

LIWO 2025.1.6 publishes candidate primary, regional, regional-water-system and outside-dike breach scenarios for professional crisis use. A catalogue marker or available tile is not a selected Hillegom event, live breach, probability or forecast.

A causal adapter must preserve release, scenario/model date, source water, defence/breach/variant, depth/velocity/arrival/duration, native CRS/resolution/units, coverage, NoData, licence, uncertainty and exercise approval before local consequences are shown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Zuid-Holland / ProRail / OVapi / NDW
evidenceSources.title: NWB N206/N207/N208/N442, N207 corridor, rail, scheduled transit and current road context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS version 9543; public context retrieved 2-3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB generates four logical GM0534 links, each with nominal 150 scenario units: N206 to Bloemendaal, N208 to Lisse, N442 to Noordwijk and N207 to Haarlemmermeer. Only mobility and supply are declared supported.

VRHM independently says N208 strongly influences Hillegom accessibility. The generated graph has no N208-labelled northbound Bloemendaal connection and instead labels that boundary edge N206, so signed-corridor continuity needs a source-geometry audit rather than assuming the four names are complete.

The province describes N207 from Hillegom toward Alphen aan den Rijn and projects affecting flow and crossings; Hillegom's eastern connection crosses the Ringvaart. Static geometry and nominal scenario units are not live bridge, road, emergency-priority, walking/cycling or freight capacity.

ProRail's manually updated CC0 register identifies Hillegom station and GTFS version 9543 contains 21 stop areas. The covered NDW snapshot assigns zero current situations to GM0534. Schedules and zero matching reports do not establish passenger presence, service, accessibility, open crossings or route availability.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / Partners in Energie; RDI; RIVM; DUO
evidenceSources.title: Electricity planning sample, antenna register, acute-care questionnaire and education locations
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 2-3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: One-postcode sampling at 2182ES identifies Liander service area OS HILLEGOM 10-1i with existing/required/queued withdrawal values 23/24/3.3 MW, fifteen queued withdrawal requests, thirteen projects and earliest project year 2026. Capacity/projects update at least quarterly and queues monthly, but the endpoint contract and exact dataset licence identifier are not stated; this is not full coverage, live load, outage or recovery.

RDI's statutory public WFS assigns 27 antenna-installation records to GM0534: nine mobile-communication, seven fixed-link and eleven radio-amateur sites. No fixed refresh or reuse licence is stated; points do not establish coverage, traffic, ownership, backhaul, power/backup, availability or restoration.

RIVM's CC0 national 2026 hospital questionnaire assigns no acute-care location inside GM0534. This means no covered respondent location intersects the boundary, not that care need is zero; cross-boundary acceptance, staffing and patient transfer remain Unknown.

DUO's daily CC-BY register assigns twelve education-use locations: seven primary, one secondary and four other registered education. Registered use does not establish people present, shelter designation, accessibility, supplies, generator endurance or operating state. All sources remain affectsSimulation=false.

evidenceSources.publisher: Interprovinciaal Overleg / Risicokaart; Register Externe Veiligheidsrisico's
evidenceSources.title: Combustible-nature eligibility and public external-safety map services
evidenceSources.edition: Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026; bounded WFS query 3 September 2026
supports: The Public Domain combustible-nature WFS returns nine forest/dune polygons in the review window, all attributed to Bloemendaal, Zandvoort or Noordwijk and none to Hillegom. They show nearby western dune/forest eligibility, but absence of a Hillegom-held polygon is a coverage/classification result, not proof that local vegetation cannot burn or that smoke cannot enter.

The layer represents static areas generally at least 100 hectares and provides no live fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, spread, wind, access, firefighting water or suppression state; feature validity begins in 2005-2012 and no operational refresh cadence is promised.

REV public WMS layers can show regulated activities, attention areas, hazardous-substance pipelines and Basisnet context. They are register/map context, not current chemical inventory, release, plume, road closure or gas-service topology; service cadence and reuse terms are not stated.

VRHM's Draka statement should be joined to a versioned REV/permit record before scenario use. Facility status, chemicals, population present and protective action remain event-time Unknowns, and sensitive operational detail must not be invented.

No identity, centre-containment, province, safety-region or headline-population contradiction was found.

Neighbourhood labels cannot identify defence failure, hydraulic compartments, sewer catchments, groundwater, culverts, vegetation fuel, plumes, buildings or service territories.

Annual CBS aggregates cannot locate event-time people, water depth, drainage failure, heat, smoke, care need, industrial inventory, household stocks or restoration priority.

Place and settlement labels are reference context only; they do not define urban drainage, Ringvaart/polder compartments, external-safety zones or service territories.
No foreign or inactive place/settlement record was found.

transport.summary: Four logical road edges are present, but signed N208 continuity, Ringvaart crossing state, rail and modal emergency capacity are not trustworthy operational topology.
notes: The graph links N208 south to Lisse, N207 east to Haarlemmermeer and N442 west to Noordwijk, but labels the north/Bloemendaal edge N206 despite VRHM identifying N208 as the major Hillegom accessibility dependency. The relevant NWB source geometry and junction grouping require audit.
Hillegom station and 21 GTFS stop areas are display context only and do not carry evacuation, patient transfer, responder or supply flow.

Nominal 150 scenario units per road are not vehicles/hour, open bridges, live passability, emergency priority or independently additive utility capacity. Zero covered NDW situations is not proof of open routes.

emergencyContext.summary: Material local water, access, care, event, external-safety and lifeline evidence remains non-causal and no operational 72-hour action ledger is present.
notes: Official deployment context assigns 24 water assets, 27 antenna sites, twelve education locations, one electricity-planning sample, zero acute-care locations and zero covered NDW situations to GM0534; all are explicitly affectsSimulation=false.

Rijnland boezem/seasonal controls, Draka/REV, Bloemencorso/transient population, N208/rail, older/less-self-reliant residents and cross-boundary care do not alter hazard, service topology or response actions.

No source reviewed supplies live shelter capacity, care occupancy/acceptance, crews, vehicles, pumps, generators, fuel, medicines, food/water stocks, household preparedness, operator switching, repair or ETA. These remain Unknown.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at six checkpoints across all eight services with complete finite output.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0534 pnpm audit:model passed one file/two tests on current code, covering ten presets × six checkpoints × eight services.

Peak severity / maximum affected / T+72 attributable person-hours are storm 0.468217 / 2,201 / 147,344.496; pluvial 0.616899 / 4,813 / 262,837.228; river 0 / 0 / 0; coastal 0.618867 / 12,752 / 764,520.612; heat 0.476521 / 275 / 107,583.171.

At T+24 coastal reports internal depth-like inundation stress 2.066345, gust 21.928955 m/s and 12,528 affected people-equivalent; compound reports rain 54.396166 mm/h, standing-water stress 0.650349, gust 23.095829 m/s and cyber 0.467065, affecting 14,100. These are synthetic exercise states, not observations or forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, reconciliation, causal closure, determinism, route ceilings and layer invariance pass.
notes: All service availability stays in [0,1]; hazards, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and event-attributable person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
For every preset/checkpoint, zero intensity gives exactly zero current/peak event severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours.
Compound T+24 has twenty-two local rows reconciling 22,786 residents, 14,100 affected people-equivalent and all eight service demand/delivery totals within tolerance.
Repeated T+24 frames are deterministic, cumulative burden is monotonic, route proxy flow respects effective capacity and all eleven map-layer selections leave numerical state invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One hazard-independent local seed overrides distinct Hillegom flood, rain, heat, fire, cyber and target geography.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have exactly the same twenty-two-neighbourhood order beginning Centrum; De Arnoud; Oranjebuurt; Patrimonium; Ringoevers and ending Om de Zanderij; Brouwerlaankwartier; Wendes; Schilderskwartier; Kastelenbuurt.

De Arnoud has zero registered residents yet ranks second for seven hazards because synthetic spatial weight and activity allocation are reused. Its positive service demand is valid after CORR-015, but that does not validate direct hazard exposure or present people.
The shared order cannot simultaneously represent Ringvaart/polder inundation, sewer/pluvial flow, heat/shade, western dune smoke, a named cyber target and a local industrial release.

Coastal proximity selects no source water/defence/breach/terrain pathway; the generic wildfire preset produces smoke 0.237629 but zero direct fire and zero affected people at T+24 without ignition, plume or wind-field evidence.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances calculate coherently, but four road proxies substitute for physical sector topology and local facility dependencies.
notes: Compound T+24 availability is power 0.331189, water 0.386901, drainage 0.294735, gas 0.552675, telecom 0.181546, mobility 0.722919, facilities 0.296312 and supply 0.664931.

NWB supports mobility and assumed road logistics only; it does not establish electricity, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, gas, telecom, care or facility connectivity. Nominal edges must not be summed as independent physical utility capacity.
Twenty-four water points and seasonal Rijnland controls establish asset and system context but not hydraulic connectivity, compatible capacity, current state, power dependence, backup or restoration.

No acute-care respondent inside GM0534 plus older/less-self-reliant and event populations makes cross-boundary access and acceptance important, but the model has no occupancy, acceptance, staff, medicine, shelter or patient-transfer ledger.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and system-pressure ledgers close and public context remains explicitly non-causal.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus ordered stage deltas sums to availability; weighted pressure contributions sum to municipal system pressure.
Drivers, dependencies and counterfactuals are finite and arithmetically closed. Household preparedness changes modeled consequence, not physical hazard fragility.

Official water, transport, antenna, care, education, grid-planning, nature and external-safety records remain affectsSimulation=false; their presence is not silently treated as live state and absence is not safety.
Arithmetic explainability does not validate the shared local seed, coastal scalar, corridor label, utility topology or exact recovery values.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent compound water avoids a false all-clear, but all dewatering, access and operator restoration magnitudes remain uncalibrated.
notes: Compound retains inundation stress 0.650349 and cyber 0.060747 at T+72, remains critical and reports 14,100 affected people-equivalent with unchanged T+24 service availability; it does not declare physical recovery.

Coastal direct forcing is zero by T+72 yet 2,828 people-equivalent remain under pressure and availability ranges from 0.626621 telecom to 0.965537 mobility without a selected hydrograph, defence closure, drainage/dewatering, access or repair model.
Storm, pluvial, winter, earthquake and wildfire forcing ends by T+72; exact service recovery percentages are deterministic assumptions, not operator forecasts or completion evidence.
No source validates Hillegom action completion, boezem/polder configuration, bridge/rail reopening, care continuity, industrial protective action, pump restoration or supply arrival.

findings.summary: Generic coastal proximity becomes precise Hillegom inundation and service impact without a selected defence/breach or Rijnland pathway.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports internal depth-like inundation stress 2.066345, critical status, 12,528 affected people-equivalent and drainage availability 0.306108. E04/E05 require source water, event-specific defence/breach, flow and compartment state; none is selected. The exact-zero river result applies only to named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing, not Ringvaart, boezem, regional kades, polders or sewers.
findings.action: Retain the coastal scalar only as a hidden non-operational diagnostic and keep the already-mitigated user-facing normalized-stress wording from CORR-017. Suppress decision-facing local affected/service consequences until a governed LIWO/Rijnland event preserves source water, defence/breach/variant, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/duration, CRS/resolution/units/NoData, uncertainty and approval. Label river zero narrowly and leave local water pathways Unknown.

findings.summary: Pluvial, sewer, groundwater, polder and boezem mechanisms are collapsed into one unsupported standing-water field.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports stress 0.630445, 4,813 affected and drainage availability 0.467857 without sewer catchments, terrain, impermeability, inlet/culvert state or pump operation. E03 says extreme rain can exceed sewer design; E04 documents event-dependent boezem decisions and seasonal De Zilk controls; E05 supplies only partial point assets.
findings.action: Separate pluvial surface runoff, sewer surcharge/overflow, groundwater, polder drainage and boezem/kade pathways. Ingest versioned 3Di/stress-test or national 70-mm scenario rasters only with native units/resolution/NoData and scenario validity; join security-safe catchments and dated Rijnland controls, otherwise use a clearly labelled synthetic range rather than precise local effect.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood exposure order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank the 22 neighbourhoods identically at T+24, with Centrum and zero-resident De Arnoud first/second and Kastelenbuurt last. E03-E08 describe mechanism-specific terrain, water, corridor, external-safety, care and nature contexts that cannot share one physical footprint.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific, source-contained spatial fields and separately allocate service demand. Preserve zero-resident activity demand from CORR-015 but never convert establishments into residents or direct exposure. Add regressions that distinct source footprints differ and event totals reconcile exactly.

findings.summary: The road graph's north boundary corridor conflicts with N208 accessibility evidence and omits operational rail/crossing state.

E06/model data contain N208 only south to Lisse while the north/Bloemendaal edge is N206; Hillegom station and 21 GTFS stops are non-causal. Four nominal 150-unit links cannot represent Ringvaart bridge state, rail, emergency priority or modal alternatives.
findings.action: Audit NWB source sections at the N206/N208 northern boundary and preserve signed physical-corridor identity. Add typed, non-additive road/bridge/rail/transit links with live-state adapters only where authoritative feeds support them; treat schedules and zero NDW matches as Unknown operational state.

findings.summary: The locally named BRZO/Seveso and hazardous-transport context has no event-valid release, plume or protective-action representation.
findings.evidence: E02 names Draka Interfoam and responder preparedness; E08 provides public REV register layers but no current inventory/release. None of the ten presets selects a Hillegom industrial or transport release, and generic smoke/cyber/service fields cannot substitute for substance, source, weather, attention area, exposed occupancy or shelter/evacuation decision.
findings.action: Create a governed external-safety scenario type using versioned REV/permit geometry plus authority-approved synthetic substance/release ranges where operational data are unavailable. Require incident time, source status, wind/plume model, uncertainty, population-time context and protective action; do not publish sensitive topology or imply the facility is active without dated confirmation.

findings.summary: Twenty-four public water assets and seasonal controls remain display-only while drainage/water recovery is precise.
findings.evidence: E05 assigns three sewer pumps, eighteen surface-water pumps and three sluices, while E04 documents dynamic boezem and De Zilk configuration. The model gives exact water/drainage availability and recovery but has no catchments, flow direction, compatible capacity units, telemetry, power/backup, failure, crew or repair state.
findings.action: Use IMWA/DAMO as attributed partial inventory only. Obtain authority-approved aggregate connectivity and event-time operational states or model explicit scenario assumptions/ranges for pumping, overflow, isolation and dewatering; retain all null capacities and missing links as Unknown.

findings.summary: Registered residents substitute for event, labour-migrant, care, school, rail and responder populations.

The model has no present-person ledger, care occupancy/acceptance, shelter activation, patient transfer, staffing or medical stocks.

Model cross-boundary acute-care acceptance, transport, shelter and supplies as constrained exercises, never infer zero need from zero RIVM locations or facility occupancy from registers.

findings.summary: Electricity, gas, telecom and supply topology, backup and restoration are replaced by road proxies and generic baselines.
findings.evidence: E07's single Liander sample reports planning/queue values and 27 antenna sites, not full topology or live state. Compound T+24 publishes exact power 0.331189, gas 0.552675 and telecom 0.181546 while the causal network has only road proxies and no feeder/switching, gas district/valve, backhaul, backup or crew data.
findings.action: Integrate public provider territories and security-safe operator aggregates with publisher/version/time/coverage/licence and distinct evidence class. Where physical topology is unavailable, use visibly synthetic zones and restoration ranges; never reuse NWB as utility topology or capacity.

findings.summary: Nearby western dune/forest eligibility is not linked to source-specific wildfire or smoke transport.
findings.evidence: E08 returns nine registered combustible-nature polygons in the review bbox, none Hillegom-held; this is not proof of local safety. The generic wildfire run has zero direct fire, smoke 0.237629 and zero affected at T+24 while using the same local order as pluvial/cyber, with no ignition, perimeter, wind, fuel, access or suppression state.
findings.action: Use Risicokaart/BRT land cover only for static eligibility and join event-valid KNMI wind plus authority ignition/perimeter/resource evidence. Separate remote smoke from direct flame, preserve cross-boundary source ownership and treat absent qualifying polygons or incidents as Unknown, not zero risk.

findings.evidence: Coastal direct forcing becomes zero by T+72 while 2,828 people-equivalent remain under pressure and exact service availability spans 0.626621-0.965537. Compound retains exactly the T+24 service vector through T+72. No reviewed source validates restoration sequencing, pump/bridge/rail status, crews, backup endurance, care continuity or supply arrival.
findings.action: Expose recovery as assumption-bounded scenarios with explicit action prerequisites, operator ownership, start/completion uncertainty and stale-data state. Never label a road, pump, facility, neighbourhood or service recovered from the preset curve alone.

findings.summary: Current public-context ingestion correctly keeps uncovered and missing observations non-causal and distinct from zero/safe.
findings.evidence: Public datasets are marked evidenceClass and affectsSimulation=false; zero acute-care locations, zero NDW situations, zero local weather/water stations, missing CBS values and no Hillegom-held combustible polygon do not change hazard or service state. CORR-017 also stops user-facing generic flood stress being labelled measured metres.
findings.action: Retain explicit Unknown/NoData/stale/unsupported states, coverage notes, retrieved/valid time and evidence class in every map, inspector, export and API. Add municipality regression assertions for zero-match layers and normalized inundation-stress wording.

findings.summary: Core deterministic, reconciliation, causal, no-event and layer-invariance contracts pass for GM0534.
findings.evidence: The focused gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values remain finite/bounded; zero intensity is exact no-event; local population/demand/delivery reconcile; deprivation is monotonic; ledgers close; repeated frames match; route ceilings hold; and map-layer selection does not alter state.
findings.action: Keep these tests as non-regression gates while correcting physical source selection, spatial allocation, network semantics and recovery; numerical coherence must never be presented as empirical validation.

corrections.summary: Introduce source-specific external-safety and cross-boundary nature-fire/smoke exercises without implying live incidents or sensitive detail.
corrections.validation: Version REV/Risicokaart/permit geometry and preserve facility status, source, valid time, coverage, licence and uncertainty. External-safety scenarios require authority-approved release/plume assumptions; fire requires ignition/perimeter, wind and fuel/suppression state; absent features/incidents remain Unknown.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, WMCN/LIWO, Rijnland, VRHM, province, municipality, infrastructure operator or emergency-service warning, forecast, probability, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration commitment.

No expert-selected Hillegom North Sea/Rijnland-boezem/Ringvaart event, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, arrival, velocity, duration/recession, verified depth units or NoData mask drives the simulation.
The exact-zero major-river result applies only to direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing; Ringvaart, boezem, regional-kade, polder, groundwater, sewer and pluvial pathways remain Unknown.
Generic floodDepthM is an internal depth-like normalized inundation-stress field; CORR-017 suppresses metre claims in user-facing surfaces, but local causal magnitude remains unsupported.

Municipal policy and current water guidance establish mechanisms/responsibilities but do not supply an event-valid reusable raster, hydraulic topology, live sewer/pump/culvert state or complete NoData contract.

The Rijnland peak-storage and De Zilk pages are dated system/operations context; they do not prove a Hillegom flood, current storage readiness, seasonal board state for an unbound scenario or guaranteed protection.
CBS generalized polygons and label points do not resolve terrain, water compartments, sewers, buildings, paving, shade, vegetation, plumes, care sites, corridors or utility service zones.

CBS neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; district heating and charging are missing everywhere and other fields partly missing. Null is Unknown, never zero service, demand, vulnerability or safety.
Registered residents exclude event visitors, workers, station passengers, pupils, care visitors and responders; no authorized event-time present-person ledger exists.
Risicokaart combustible-nature polygons are static eligibility and none is Hillegom-held in the bounded query; absence does not prove no local fuel or cross-boundary smoke.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish live N206/N207/N208/N442, Ringvaart bridge, rail, bus, walking/cycling, evacuation, emergency-priority or freight status/capacity.
Zero covered NDW situations is no covered report at snapshot time, not proof that roads, crossings or rail are open.
IMWA/DAMO point assets do not establish full hydraulic connectivity, compatible capacity units, control logic, telemetry, current operation, power backup, crews or repair.
The NBNL postcode lookup is one Liander planning sample, not full municipality/feeder coverage, live load, switching, outage, emergency reserve or restoration.
Antenna points do not establish coverage, operator ownership, backhaul, traffic, power/backup or restoration; no complete public gas or telecom operational topology is authorized.

Zero RIVM acute-care respondent locations is a coverage fact, not zero care need; live hospital acceptance, care occupancy, staff, medicines, shelters, generators and transfer capacity remain Unknown.
VRHM and REV/permit context do not establish a current Draka status, chemical inventory, release, plume, exposed occupancy or protective action; sensitive detail must not be invented.
Cyber disruption has no named target, architecture, attack/detection/containment state or authoritative operational evidence; generic service loss is not an observed incident.
No validated inventory is available for shelters, pumps/generators, fuel, food/water/medicine stocks, crews, vehicles, mutual aid, household preparedness or completed actions.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, injury, mortality, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss; 72 hours excludes prolonged contamination and reconstruction.

Zuid-Holland/RWS/municipality/VRHM/ProRail/operators: audit N206/N208 northern source geometry, N207 Ringvaart crossing, N442, rail/transit and emergency/care continuity without turning schedules or static geometry into capacity.

Zuid-Holland/VRHM/municipality/REV/Omgevingsdienst: validate current Draka/other regulated-activity status and authority-approved release/plume/protective-action exercises while withholding sensitive operational detail.

Zuid-Holland/VRHM/municipality/Noord-Holland partners: validate cross-boundary western dune/forest smoke, ignition, access and suppression pathways; no Hillegom-held Risicokaart polygon must not be interpreted as safe.

Zuid-Holland/operators/municipality/Rijnland: validate security-safe aggregate water, wastewater, electricity, gas, telecom and facility zones, dependencies, backup and restoration ranges; never reuse NWB as utility topology or convert missing data into zero/safe.

Zuid-Holland/CBS/municipality/VRHM/care/event partners: keep registered residents separate from Bloemencorso, labour-migrant, school, rail, care and responder populations and validate privacy-safe shelter, care acceptance and supply continuity for T+0 to T+72.
